title: Routing policy grammar rework for multi-region and tiered fallbacks
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Refactor the routing policy engine DSL and its configuration schema to support deterministic region selection, explicit tier routing, and graceful fallback to compatible model variants. Current issues: ad-hoc rule ordering causes non-deterministic routing across regions, tier matching overlaps with capacity policies, and fallback logic is duplicated across runtime components. This ticket scopes a grammar redesign, validator/compiler stages, and a migration path for existing customer policies. Goals: 1) Define a concise DSL grammar that makes region/tier/fallback semantics explicit, 2) Implement a typed AST and staged validators (syntactic, semantic, compatibility), 3) Provide runtime-compatible compiled artifacts and a safe migration strategy that supports 'legacy' and 'compiled' modes during rollout.
acceptance_criteria: New DSL grammar spec published and reviewed by PM/Design/Infra
Parser implemented with unit tests covering >95% grammar cases
Typed AST produced by compiler and passes semantic validation for region, tier, and fallback nodes
Config validator detects and rejects ambiguous or non-deterministic rules with clear error messages
Runtime can load compiled policy artifacts and fall back to textual rules without requiring rolling restarts
Migration harness executed against 50 production-like policies without customer-visible routing changes unless policy is intentionally updated
Performance: policy compile+validation latency < 15ms on CI VM; runtime eval overhead < 2% at p99 compared to baseline
implementation_notes: Language: Rust for compiler and parser (reuse existing runtime FFI bindings). Parser generator: pest or nom — prototype with pest for clarity, then evaluate nom for perf if necessary.
Phases: parse -> typed AST -> semantic validator -> canonicalizer -> bytecode/serialized policy for runtime
Region selection semantics: explicit 'region' clause with optional 'preferred' list. If multiple regions match, tie-breaker order is explicit in rule weight, not insertion order.

Tier routing: introduce 'tier' primitive (e.g., premium, standard, best-effort) with numeric priority and capacity hints. Tier rules are orthogonal to region rules; compiler produces composite selectors.

Fallback model variants: allow 'fallback' chains with compatibility predicates (architecture, runtime-compat, quantization). Compiler must ensure fallback variants are strictly compatible or mark policy invalid.
Backward compatibility: runtime accepts both legacy textual policies and compiled artifacts. Add a feature flag 'routing.compiled.enabled' to toggle compiled path per deployment.
Validation levels: 'syntax' (parse), 'constraints' (schema types and ranges), 'safety' (conflicting fallbacks, circular fallback chains), 'compat' (model variant compatibility against catalog)
Errors: produce user-facing errors with code, hint, and link to remediation docs (confluence://team/routing/dsl-errors).
Observability: emit policy-compile metrics (duration, errors), and annotate evaluation traces with rule-id and compilation-hash for debugging and audits.
Testing: unit parser tests, property-based tests for canonicalization, e2e with runtime in docker-compose harness, and chaos test for failing region endpoints to exercise fallbacks.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable compiled path in staging clusters and compile existing policies; verify no behavioral diffs using policy-diff harness
Phase 2 (gradual): enable compiled path for 10% of production traffic; monitor eval traces and fallback rates for anomalies
Phase 3 (opt-in): provide a 'migrate' CLI that upgrades customer policies to the new DSL with warnings for any incompatible constructs
Phase 4 (rollout): flip global feature flag once telemetry shows parity; continue to accept legacy textual policies for 3 months before requiring migration
Rollback: if compiled path causes regressions, toggle 'routing.compiled.enabled=false' which falls back to textual interpreter without restarting services
tests_and_validation: Integration: runtime load compiled policy and compare outputs vs legacy interpreter across 200 synthetic workloads
Compatibility: validate fallback chains against model-catalog snapshot (include quantization and kernel constraints)
Performance: benchmark compile and evaluation against baseline for 1k rules dataset
Safety: create fuzzing harness to target circular fallback detection and large-disjunction explosion
docs_and_links: Model catalog snapshot used for compat tests: s3://redwood-model-catalog/snapshots/2026-03-05.json
tradeoffs: Using Rust increases compile-time integration but reduces runtime bugs vs a dynamic-language implementation
Introducing compiled artifacts improves performance and clearer errors but requires migration and dual-mode complexity
Explicit grammar reduces accidental overlaps but increases the verbosity of simple rules; we'll provide a converter to ease authoring
Stricter validation may break some customer policies; we mitigate with a migration and detailed error messages
blockers: Dependency: model-catalog API contract update required to expose 'compatibility fingerprints' (ENG-21890)
Need security sign-off for new serialized policy format (security review in progress)
Resource: small Rust compiler expertise gap on the team — plan to pair with infra-engineering for initial implementation
